questions.question: Explain what a catchment is and why the health of a river reflects its whole catchment.
questions.expected_answer: A catchment (drainage basin) is the area of land from which rainwater drains into a river and its tributaries, bounded by the watershed (high ground). Parts include source, tributaries, confluence, main channel, mouth/estuary. Runoff from farms, towns, mines and forests carries soil, chemicals, litter and sewage into streams, so land use throughout the catchment affects water quality and flow; wetlands store water, reduce floods and filter pollutants.

questions.question: Describe signs of healthy and unhealthy rivers and how miniSASS is used to assess river health.
questions.expected_answer: Healthy: clear water, enough oxygen, natural flow, natural banks with indigenous vegetation, varied habitats, many species. Unhealthy: murky/discoloured, bad smell, foam/oil, algae (eutrophication), dead fish, litter, eroded banks, alien plants, few species. miniSASS: collect invertebrates by disturbing stones in front of a net; identify groups; each has a sensitivity score (stoneflies, mayflies sensitive; worms, leeches tolerant); the average score gives the river's condition (natural to very poor); results can be mapped online.

questions.question: Identify threats to South Africa's rivers and suggest ways to care for catchment areas.
questions.expected_answer: Threats: failing sewage works, fertilisers/pesticides, industrial waste, acid mine drainage, litter; invasive alien plants (wattle, eucalyptus, pine, water hyacinth); dams and abstraction changing flow; loss of half or more of wetlands, bank clearing, sand mining; soil erosion; climate change. Care: ecological reserve, catchment management agencies, fines, Green Drop/Blue Drop; Working for Water and Working for Wetlands; buffer strips, careful chemical use, keeping livestock off banks, contour ploughing; treating industrial and mine water; clean-ups, not dumping, reporting pollution, planting indigenous trees, miniSASS monitoring, enviro-champs, adopt-a-stream.
